# Khaine’s Eyes

*Pages PDF 91-98*

## **Khaine’s Eyes**
## **A Fortuitous Encounter**
Bound by a single, cruel will, Khaine’s Eyes have become indispensable scouts and guerrilla fighters for _Temple of Spite_ . Whether that can hold this fierce band together much longer is another matter. 

The sorceress Samuril Meurlith had done well in the vicious politics of the Dark Convent, where even survival is an accomplishment. Her meteoric rise through the ranks of the powerful in Ghrond has left a trail of corpses, so much so that her jealous superiors, fearing they might be next, decided to get rid of her by tasking her with a dangerous and difficult mission: to bring back the head of the renegade sorcerer Kernethar Grimwitch, last seen in the Old World. Her enemies in the Dark Convent assumed this task would prove too hazardous for Samuril, but little do they realise that she has proved a capable survivor and the leader of the arks’ scouting forces. 

In 2510 IC, Samuril journeyed to Karond Kar, following rumours of fugitive elves she hoped might provide clues to Grimwitch’s whereabouts. She was able to get passage aboard _Temple of Spite_ easily enough, as Duriath was pleased to have an experienced sorceress join his crew. Exploring the depths of the ark, Samuril uncovered a band of Autarii Shades lurking in a remote cavern, a band of half-starved fugitives who had fallen foul of their chief and were in hiding. Seizing the opportunity, she slew one of the Shades to display her sorcerous might and demanded the fealty of the survivors. Clearly impressed, the Shades agreed to serve Samuril if she helped them exact revenge against their old chief. The surviving Autarii vaunted her with reverence, claiming that she was favoured by Hekarti. 

Submitting herself and her followers to Helbane, Samuril offered her service. The fleetmaster needed a new scouting force after several Shades were lost in the jungles of Lustria. He accepted her offer, especially as her actions would unsettle the other sorceresses and make them less likely to plot against him. Granting her the service of a small contingent of dark riders, Helbane named them Khaine’s Eyes. 

## **Goals**
**Serve Duriath Helbane.** The Shades and dark riders know that first and foremost, they have a duty to the fleetmaster, whether they like it or not. The first time anyone forgets that is the last time. Samuril ensures the fleetmaster is kept happy as insurance against the other sorceresses taking overt action against her. 

**Inflict terror on lesser species.** For the Shades, led by Gref, their aim is simple. They wish to revel in cruelty, kill, and consume the hearts of enemies in sacrifice to Khaine. They try to take captives on every mission, unless explicitly ordered otherwise. Even then, they obey grudgingly. 

**Scout for the warhost.** Khaine’s Eyes primary purpose is to scout ahead of any military engagements by the ark’s warhost. They map territory, track enemy movements, and build intelligence of troop dispositions and garrison strengths. They are expected to weaken opposition when the opportunity presents itself. 

**Hunt Kernethar Grimwitch.** Samuril has orders from the Dark Convent to find and kill the renegade sorcerer. She plans to bypass the ark’s coven and Ghrond’s supreme sorceresses to present Grimwitch’s head to Malerion herself, and with his gratitude rise in the order, subservient only to Morathi.. 

## **On the Black Ark**
Aboard _Temple of Spite_ , Khaine’s Eyes have claimed the abandoned chambers where Samuril discovered the Shade clan. Deep within the Depths, Samuril maintains her rooms, visiting the Mistborne Vigil only when required. Surrounded by awestruck Autarii frightened of her wrath, she is, for now, safe from murderous designs. The dark riders have quarters nearby, their steeds stabled in rooms that once belonged to a forgotten noble. Captives tend the mounts, and sometimes become their food. 

The Eyes spend little time on the black ark, regularly setting out with various reaver fleets. Even when on board, they are not idle. The Autarii cannot resist the urge to hunt, and the alleys, courtyards, and corridors of _Temple of Spite_ ring with their cries as they prey upon any captives unlucky enough to cross their path. On occasion, they hunt Druchii servants they perceive as threats to Samuril, chasing them into the depths for the kill. 

To amuse themselves between missions, the dark riders organise competitions on deck. They favour a form of mounted sport in which the object is to spear a human head and then carry it across a goal line before other riders can intercept and steal it. Played against other teams of dark riders, the matches can end in deadly combat. 

## **Rivals and Allies**
Knowing she needs allies, Samuril assiduously cultivates alliances of mutual interest with other factions on _Temple of Spite_ . While the Shades are her loyal bodyguards, she can only be assured of their support whilst she provides them with the sort of leadership that sees them secure victories and captives. 

The Eyes also associate with the beastmasters who live in the depths, who themselves are often held in contempt by Druchii highborn as glorified ostlers. Samuril exploits this to bind her to them in mutual animosity toward the other sorceresses and, through High Beastmaster Scaleflayer, she hopes to acquire more steeds to augment her forces. 

Harzeth Duskmantle of the Glass Thorn knows of Samuril’s attempts to recruit her own spies and resents her encroaching on his territory. Should she ever seriously threaten to rival his own accomplishments, he will endeavour to see her discredited and humiliated. If bringing about the sorceress’s disgrace proves too complicated, Harzeth will not be above plotting her death. 

## **In the Old World**
Khaine’s Eyes feel no need to hide that they are Druchii, not that Autarii would be willing or capable of doing so. Neither do they announce their identity to their victims. The confusion caused by survivors claiming they were attacked by elves serves to keep their enemies off-guard. 

Though the Eyes go wherever Helbane commands, Samuril pushes to keep their focus on the Old World. Following her divinations, the Eyes are most active from the Empire to Estalia and Tilea, looking for any trace of Kernethar Grimwitch. The Eyes have ventured as far up the Reik as Altdorf where, on a recent Geheimnisnacht, they dared to infiltrate the city itself. The few who caught glimpses of skulking elves were written off as superstitious drunks. The spy Dalaethra Bladeborn (page 89) was furious, but they were gone before she could act. 

Khaine’s Eyes never forget their role on _Temple of Spite_ . Arriving days ahead of an army, they move fast and far, probing and misdirecting the enemy’s defences. Once the work is done, a dark rider races back to report to the main force. Sometimes Samuril gives the Autarii free rein, and the inhabitants of a village or a small castle die in an orgy of blood. These atrocities do more than placate the Shades, they draw attention from where the main blow will fall. 

## **Meeting Khaine’s Eyes**
Off the ark, encounters with Khaine’s Eyes usually involve dealing with a roving band of Shades, a confrontation which often ends in violence or a chase. If the Characters are unfortunate enough to spend the night where the Eyes are reconnoitring, the dark elves try and kill them and harvest their hearts. 

Meeting Khaine’s Eyes can present a dilemma. The Characters might come upon the aftermath of a raid and discover that survivors were abducted a short while ago. In such cases, is it better to rescue the captives or warn nearby towns of the danger? 

If the Characters are near Marienburg or another Old World city, Khaine’s Eyes could appear in pursuit of Kernethar Grimwitch. They could protect him and gain a useful, though despicable ally, or offer him to Samuril and earn fleeting gratitude from a thoroughly evil elf. 

On the other hand, the hunters could become the hunted. The Eyes have been spotted, and the local garrison needs to know where the reavers will land so they can direct their gathering troops to the right place. The mission becomes one of stealth, as the Characters must find the Shades or the dark riders and trail them rather than engaging with them. If the Eyes can be tracked stealthily, they may give away the position of a site from which they can rendezvous with one of Helbane’s corsair captains. 

## **Disposition**
Khaine’s Eyes comprises of Shades, dark riders, and their leader, Samuril. In battle, they rarely engage an enemy directly, preferring to fire on them or ambush them from the rear. 

- **Sorceress Samuril Meurlith** , her apprentice **Nyssara** , and her familiar, a daemonic imp she calls Lior. The sorceress usually rides a dark steed when away from the ark. 

## **Appearance**
The Shades present a fearsome sight: dressed in leathers made from tanned human or elf skins they paint themselves with red and black pigments to appear daemonic, and some even wear leather masks made from the faces of slain foes. Kalimel’s riders are famous for the raven feather cloaks they wear, as well as their deadly accuracy with repeater crossbows. 

## **Deal with a Daemon — Easy Encounter**
A dark rider fled the scouting band when they were surprised by a State Army patrol. The Characters were dispatched to pursue him, as he carries documents bearing defensive plans and army dispositions. If the dark elves receive this information, it could be fatal for those defending the region. The Characters can eventually corner the rider if they make haste and chase him into a closed gorge nearby. A difficult fight looms, not only against the dark elf, but his hellish mount. It is at this moment that he offers them a deal. 

The rider introduces himself as Zaurith. He is loyal to Kalimel rather than the sorceress who consorts with primitive Shades. He shares Kalimel’s goal of weakening Samuril’s position and splitting the riders away from the Autarii. If this means many dark elves will die, well, so be it. Zaurith is even ready to risk his own life if it means liberty for his fellow riders. 

Zaurith offers to give up the documents and even submit to a clean death, if only the Characters will first attack the remaining Shades who are camped nearby. Zaurith claims that there are just four Shades in the camp, with three captive soldiers trussed up (all have a _Fatigued_ Condition). If the Characters trust Zaurith they will find the situation is exactly as he says, but why an elf would willingly seek the destruction of his fellows remains a mystery. 

- **Gref** , the Autarii headman, leader of the Shades. He is accompanied by 12 of his closest kinsmen, many of them his siblings or cousins. 

- A band of 20 Shades who call themselves the **Moonhaunters** . The Bloodshade who leads them is Gref ’s uncle, who divides them into three units of six or seven when scouting. 

- The **Triple-scarred** are a loose band of 30 Shades who form and reform into different skirmishing parties as needed. They melt into the night and signal one another with the cry of the Naggarothi doomwing. 

- **Yasl’s Band** are aloof. These 13 Autarii prefer silence and their own company to the rest of the Shades. Yasl herself rarely shows an expression other than contempt. 

- **Kalimel Nightpiercer** leads the dark riders, the 11 who survived death in Lustria. 

## **Blades in the Night — Medium Encounter**
Somewhere along the stormy coasts of the Old World, Khaine’s Eyes scout the region for raiders arriving in three days. The Moonhaunters, a band of 20 Shades, has found the village where the Characters are staying. Unrestrained by their leader, the Druchii decide reconnaissance is not enough, Khaine demands blood and hearts! 

The first warning comes with a scream in the night and the sound of the temple bell ringing an alarm, which is suddenly cut off. People run around, making seemingly nonsensical claims that ‘elves are attacking’ the village. Characters who take to the streets find a scene of chaos, there is panic in the streets, the scant militia struggling to mobilise, and groups of elves, their faces painted, battering down doors and dragging people away. 

The task becomes one of survival and saving who they can. The Characters could send a desperate signal to a nearby knightly chapterhouse, only 20 minutes’ ride away. They could rally the villagers to lead a counterattack, or they can gather survivors and hold out in a strong building, such as the town inn. There are fewer Shades than it first appears and the 12 Druchii believe they have the upper hand. 

Assuming they survive, morning brings a new challenges. Did any raiders escape? What do the Characters do with the survivors? Can they rescue the missing? Why were the Shades in the area anyway? 

## **Bring Me the Head of Grimwitch! — Hard Encounter**
Captured in a raid, the Characters are prisoners aboard _Temple of Spite_ . After days spent in the cells, guards come for them and bring them chained before the sorceress Damuril. 

She does not make them an offer. They are now her property. Discerning their abilities and ability to blend in with the locals, she gives them a mission. A Druchii ship will take them to the coast of the Wasteland, whence they must make their way to Marienburg. There they are to track down a renegade Dark Elf named Kernethar Grimwitch (see page 124), a sorcerer, and bring him, or at least his head, back to her. To ensure their obedience, she has each Character branded with a rune. Should they betray her, the magic in the rune will crush their hearts when Mannslieb is next full — in two weeks’ time. If they obey, she will set them free. 

In Marienburg, Samuril’s information leads to the Elf Quarter and the nearby districts, but provides nothing more specific. Investigation eventually uncovers the renegade sorcerer but may also attract the attention of the elven guards (the ManniocsQuinsh), Marienburg’s Black Caps, and several ‘information specialists’ in the city, who will become very curious about their activities. Grimwitch may prove useful in his own right. He wants to be left alone, though if the Characters treat with him carefully he can use his sorcery to remove the runes. 

## **Ladrielle, Lady of Mists**
Ladrielle is the protectress of all things that are hidden or lost, and patron of travellers in the wilderness. By tradition, she is the only goddess who still walks in the mortal world, defying the will of Asuryan with a confident flagrance, and there are tales told of her coming to the aid of those lost in the mists of yvresse or upon the trackless ocean. her worship is observed in those cities, such as Lothern and Tor yvresse, where elven wanderlust has never faded, but there her supplicants are careful in their petitions, for as one of the Cytharai, Ladrielle is considered by most sensible asur to be a dangerous goddesss to court openly. Ladrielle’s face is always hidden behind a veil, but many elves assume she is the most beautiful of all goddesses. Others, however, suspect that she is merely a guise adopted by another deity, one whose true identity is hidden behind the ashen silk. 

in naggaroth, the chief shrine to Ladrielle can be found on the coast to the north of the Granite hills. Unlike the high elves, the Druchii court her blessings openly, for they do not fear to honour the gods and goddesses of the underworld. in particular, many shades offer their prayers to goddess, for as a protectress of the lost and guardian of travellers, she befits both their history as fugitives and lifestyle as dwellers of the wilds. 

## **Gref, Autarii Headman**
Gref should be dead and knows it. He was the right hand of Malathnil, who tried to kill the former headman of his Autarii clan on the black ark. The attempt failed when the headman discovered the plot, and the rebels fled and hid within in the remote corners of the Depths. In the bowels of the ark, they were found by a lone sorceress, Samuril, who demonstrated her power by killing Malathnil with a word. Rather than take revenge, Gref fell to the floor to worship her as Hekarti’s Chosen, which she proved by leading them in revenge against the old chief. Killing him, she claimed the Shades as her servants and named Gref their new headman. 

Gref is fearsome, even for a Shade. He dresses in leather made from the skin of his human victims, sometimes flayed from them before they die. His arms and face are tattooed and scarred, giving him a daemonic appearance, reminiscent of a fiend from the Chaos Wastes rather than an elf. Though he carries a Druchii sword and crossbow, his favoured weapon is an obsidian knife, razor sharp and perfect for making a new outfit of flayed flesh.

## **Kalimel Nightpiercer, Dark Rider**
Kalimel of Naggarond dreams the same two dreams every night. In the first, he is second-in-command of a scouting force from _Temple of Spite_ , lost in Lustria’s Mosquito Swamp, surrounded by lizardmen and their beasts. Their doom is at hand, and the dream ends as blood and brains from his leader’s shattered skull rain down upon his face. 

The other dream features him in command of a new unit of dark riders, their banners granted by Duriath Helbane and consecrated with the blood of the sorceress Meurlith, who lies trampled and dying under his mount. This second dream has kept him alive in the years since Helbane formed Khaine’s Eyes. 

Tall for a Druchii, Kalimel cuts an impressive figure even among Dark Riders. Riding atop his steed, Bloodwind, with his sword raised as his raven cloak billows behind him, many a foe has thought a daemon was upon them. Kalimel is a skilled horseman, known for moving with almost impossible speed. He and Bloodwind are a perfect team, the horse knowing where he wants to go while Kalimel fights.

## **Samuril Meurlith, Sorceress**
It is said that Morathi ordered the exile of Samuril from Ghrond, but the sorceress cannot fathom the Hag Queen of Ghrond’s motives. To Samuril, the reason makes no difference. To survive, she needs her own power base outside of the Dark Convent. To win, she must gain Malerion’s favour by taking credit for eliminating Kernethar Grimwitch. Then she can return, destroy her enemies, and find a place at Morathi’s side. First she must use her spies to discern the renegade sorcerer’s location, then lead Khaine’s Eyes into hostile territory to capture Grimwitch. 

Samuril is of medium height for a dark elf, a mature adult whose jet black hair flows to her waist. Her face is pretty and a wide, charming smile comes easily to her lips; her expression conceals her burgeoning arrogance and a will to command that brooks no defiance. Though dressed in the robes of a sister of the Dark Convent on _Temple of Spite_ , off the vessel she wears the leathers of the Autarii and the raven cloak of the dark riders, showing her mastery of both. She bears no weapon other than her dagger, for her sorcery is potent enough. 

She is an active leader, pursuing her own goal whilst being careful to keep Duriath Helbane satisfied.

## **The Orchestra of Tides**
samuril is plotting a sorcerous spectacular, a ritual masterpiece to resonate as far as Ghrond and attract the attention of Kernethar Grimwitch. By planting a series of rune-etched stones along the Ostland coastline, she will perform a ritual that alters the flow of time. Folk in several villages will start aging years in hours and buildings will crumble into ruins. The Characters discover the shades and dark riders as they bury stones in the cliffs as samuril sings incantations from a promontory. as the spell takes form, the Characters experience strange accelerations of time, pockets of reversing or frozen time, and memories rearranged. Can the Characters act before they forget their purpose entirely? 

## **The Spirals**
small patrols of state troops are going missing from their camps at night. Their tents and campfires are left intact, while all that remains of the soldiers are trails of loose teeth arranged in spiral patterns. This is an old autarii custom, wreathed in superstition and representing a deliberate taunt to their victims. Gref carefully arranges for each spiral of teeth to trace a trail which forms a larger spiral. at the centre of the trail, he and his shades lie in wait for the Characters if they were ‘intelligent’ enough to fall into his trap 

## **Keeping an Eye Out**
## **Shade for Sale**
Once a month, norderingen plays hosts to pit bosses from across Middenland who meet at night for a secret auction, where adversaries and beasts are sold for their stables. amongst the usual beastmen, goblins, and norscans is an unusual and valuable fighter — a vicious elf with a shaved head and streaks of terrifying paint across his face. This is nyran, one of Khaine’s eyes who was captured during a raid in nordland. The Characters happen across the auction and hear the dark elf whisper an offer to them. Buy his freedom and his headman will repay them in silver and vengeance against their enemies. 

Around the coasts of the Old World and Araby, Samuril maintains a web of human contacts, or ‘Eyes for the Eyes’ as she calls them. Few of these secret agents realise that they are dealing with a Druchii, let alone one the feared sorceressses of Ghrond, but what does it matter to them when there is a pouch of gold to be earned, or vengeance wreaked against another? Short-sighted as well as short-lived, humans almost never consider the wider consequences until they themselves are trapped by them. 

Samuril deploys the dark riders to find and approach potential agents, as Shades are not usually renowned for their skill with honeyed words and patient negotiation. Typically a rider scouts and observes a potential target for days or even weeks before making contact. One night, a voice from the shadows offers satisfaction, or threatens blackmail, but always promises gold in return for cooperation. 

The network of human contacts has a dual function, to extend the reach of the band’s scrutiny of potential enemies and to provide Samuril with scraps of information which could lead to Kernethar Grimwitch.
